_strings.@@44cf3cd04649: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Residents who qualified for and claimed the federal child and dependent care credit on federal Form 2441 (care expenses for a qualifying child/dependent so the taxpayer can work). If you did not meet federal filing requirements but would have been entitled to the federal credit, you may still claim the Kentucky credit by completing federal Form 2441 and stating on the form 'did not meet federal filing requirements.' Kentucky has no separate income limit; eligibility tracks the federal credit.

Kentucky law requires the individual income tax return to begin with federal adjusted gross income and be adjusted for any differences to arrive at Kentucky adjusted gross income, so the conformity date governs which federal provisions flow through and which are modified on Schedule M (special depreciation/Section 179 differences, federal NOL, the Kentucky excess business loss limitation, etc.). _strings.@@7bf78ac42949: Treaty conformity — KY conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from KY income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the KY return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Kentucky's resident return (Form 740) starts from federal adjusted gross income — 2024 Form 740 line 5 is federal AGI ("Enter the total amount of your federal adjusted gross income from your federal income tax return... Do not confuse federal adjusted gross income with federal taxable income"), and the 2024 packet states Kentucky law "requires that the individual income tax return begin with federal adjusted gross income and be adjusted for any differences to arrive at Kentucky adjusted gross income." Modifications are made on Schedule M. The 2024 Schedule M "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" (Part I, lines 1-5, totaled on line 6) are: (1) interest on other states' obligations / taxable mutual-fund dividends, (2) resident adjustment from Kentucky Schedule K-1, (3) special depreciation/Section 179 differences, (4) federal net operating loss, and (5) "other additions" (reservist/National Guard expenses, lump-sum distribution 20% capital-gains portion, passive activity loss adjustment, pension/IRA basis differences, intangible-asset and post-9/10/2001 depreciable-property gain differences, Armed Forces moving expenses, Kentucky excess business loss limitation). NONE of these add back federally tax-treaty-exempt income. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and KY has no add-back for it, it is not re-taxed by Kentucky — therefore KY conforms.

_strings.@@a528bcefc4c5: Personal Tax Credits (age 65+, blind, or Kentucky National Guard) — Taxpayer (and spouse, if filing jointly or married filing separately on a combined return) who, as of 12/31/2024, was age 65 or older, was legally blind, and/or was a member of the Kentucky National Guard. A taxpayer can claim more than one (e.g., 65+ AND blind). No income limit.

_strings.@@b88acf8e41ea: Family Size Tax Credit — Resident individuals/families with modified gross income (MGI) at or below 133% of the federal poverty threshold for their family size. Family size is capped at 4 (yourself, spouse if living in same household, and qualifying children). Available even to someone claimed as a dependent on a parent's return (family size 1). To get ANY credit, 2024 MGI must be at or below $20,030 (family of 1), $27,185 (family of 2), $34,341 (family of 3), or $41,496 (family of 4+) — the packet's line 20/21 instructions say "If your total MGI is $41,496 or less, you may qualify."

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: Form 740 Line 12 = Line 11 (Taxable Income = Line 9 Kentucky AGI minus Line 10 deduction) x four percent (.04) — printed on the 2024 form: "Tax Computation: Multiply line 11 by 4% (.04)". Line 5 starts from federal AGI ("Do not confuse federal adjusted gross income with federal taxable income"). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate change: the 2024 rate is 4% (.04), down from 4.5% in 2023 (2024 packet What's New); the standard deduction rose to $3,160 (from $2,980). Kentucky allows ONE $3,160 standard deduction per return — a joint return gets a single $3,160 (it is NOT doubled); spouses filing separately on a combined return (Filing Status 2) get $3,160 each column. Kentucky has no personal or dependent exemptions; the nonrefundable personal tax credits ($40 age 65+, $40 blind, $20 Kentucky National Guard — 2024 Schedule ITC Section B) and the Family Size Tax Credit (Form 740 lines 20-21) are CREDITS against tax and are NOT modeled by calc.state_tax — compute them on Schedule ITC / the Family Size Tax Credit Table. Kentucky local occupational license taxes (county/city payroll taxes) are NOT modeled.
